key_insight: A retrieval-augmented foundation model trained on large-scale matched molecular pair transformations (MMPTs) uses a variable-to-variable formulation to generate diverse, controllable analogs that recapitulate medicinal chemistry intuition.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between whole-molecule generative models (which lack local-edit controllability) and small, restricted MMP learners by offering scalable, chemistry-aware analog generation that produces realistic, locally focused edits.
method: Variable-to-variable formulation: treat analog generation as mapping an input chemical variable (local context/fragment) to diverse output variables (candidate edits).
Foundation-model pretraining on a large corpus of MMPTs to learn common medicinal-chemistry transformations and priors for realistic edits.
Retrieval augmentation: fetch contextually similar MMP examples from a database at inference to bias generation toward well-established, chemistry-plausible edits and increase diversity/control.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners and cheminformaticians to generate realistic, controllable molecular analogs at scale—improving lead optimization, interpretability, and transfer across projects by leveraging learned medicinal-chemistry patterns and retrievals.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: database of MMPs -> retrieval module -> foundation model -> diverse output analogs, with highlighted local edits.
Before/after molecular examples: matched molecular pair snapshots showing precise local substitution and chemical rationale.
Bar/line chart: comparison of edit controllability, chemical validity, and diversity versus baseline whole-molecule and small-MMP models.
Schematic of retrieval attention: nearest-neighbor MMPs influencing generated edits (illustrates how retrieval guides model decisions).
paper_title: Retrieval-Augmented Foundation Models for Matched Molecular Pair Transformations to Recapitulate Medicinal Chemistry Intuition
paper_authors: Bo Pan, Peter Zhiping Zhang, Hao-Wei Pang, Alex Zhu, Xiang Yu
